newsitem.title: INDIA: Suspected guerrillas kill 17 in attack in India.
newsitem.headline: Suspected guerrillas kill 17 in attack in India.

text.p: Suspected separatist militants killed 17 people and wounded 20 in an attack on a village in the northeastern Indian state of Tripura, police said on Wednesday.

Guerrillas belonging to the All Tripura Tiger Force, which is fighting for a separate nation, set fire to about 40 homes in Jarul Bachai in the western section of the state, then fired on fleeing residents, police in the state capital Agartala said.

Fifteen of the victims were killed on the spot while two died in hospital, a police officer told Reuters in the eastern city of Calcutta by telephone. Ten of the 20 wounded were in critical condition in hospital, he said.
Paramilitary forces were searching for the attackers, the police official said.

Last July, the All Tripura Tiger Force issued a statement warning Bengali settlers to leave the state, which borders Bangladesh. The group's militants have killed about 35 people in the past two months, authorities said.
The attack occurred late on Tuesday near the Khowai region where on Sunday more than 60 houses were set on fire in ethnic clashes between tribals and Bengali settlers.
The state government imposed a curfew on the Khowai region after Sunday's fighting.
On February 6, five people were killed in Khowai in ethnic clashes and police firing.

Tripura has an 840-km (520-mile) border with Bangladesh to the west. The state's indigenous tribal population has been reduced to a minority by Bengali Hindu immigrants who now dominate local politics and the economy.
More than 2,000 people were killed in the region's worst ethnic riots in June 1980.
